explanation: The theorem is `Module.Finite (ZMod p) (P0 →+ ZMod p)` for a module P0 that is finite over ℤ_[p]. It is proved by the library's own `moduleFinite_hom`. That lemma needs a real argument: it reduces to the ℤ_[p]-generators of P0 and uses p • x = 0 in ZMod p. I grepped Mathlib for `Module.Finite` statements about `→+` and found only `Module.Finite.addMonoidHom`. That declaration concerns ℤ-modules, so it gives finiteness over ℤ and not over ZMod p. It also needs `Module.Finite ℤ` on the target, with the other side only a free finite-rank module, and P0 is not finite over ℤ here. I found no Mathlib declaration that gives the ZMod p-finiteness of additive homomorphisms out of a ℤ_[p]-finite module, either directly or in a short derivation.
